core_obligations: Check additivity of the auxiliary quantity: on the category of 2-periodic complexes whose M and N have finite length, the expression length_R(M) - length_R(N) is additive in short exact sequences, so that it may be compared with e_R (proof lines 268-270).

Insert the displayed short exact sequence 0 -> (M, Im(phi), phi, 0) -> (M, N, phi, psi) -> (0, N/Im(phi), 0, 0) -> 0, whose first terms are the ones where psi vanishes and whose third term has trivial M; combining the initial remark with additivity of e_R (tag 0EA7) reduces the identity to the two cases (a) M = 0 and (b) phi surjective (proof lines 271-278).

Draw the two consequences: the stated formula e_R(M, N, phi, psi) = length_R(M) - length_R(N), and the vanishing of e_R(M, phi, psi) for a (2,1)-periodic complex of finite length, which is the special case N = M with psi = 0 (proof lines 278-279).
proof_roadmap: Record that length_R(M) - length_R(N) is additive in short exact sequences on complexes with finite-length M and N (proof lines 268-270).
Split off the subcomplex (M, Im(phi), phi, 0) and the quotient (0, N/Im(phi), 0, 0), which turns the claim into the two cases M = 0 and phi surjective (proof lines 271-278).
Conclude for the two-periodic and then for the (2,1)-periodic case (proof lines 278-279).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the multiplicity of a 2-periodic complex of finite-length modules as the alternating sum of the lengths of M and N, and deduces the vanishing of e_R for (2,1)-periodic complexes (statement lines 259-264). The proof does not compute the two remaining cases directly but instead observes that length_R(M) - length_R(N) is additive on the category of complexes with finite-length M and N, then splits off the displayed short exact sequence 0 -> (M, Im(phi), phi, 0) -> (M, N, phi, psi) -> (0, N/Im(phi), 0, 0) -> 0, which isolates exactly the cases where the assertion is immediate (proof lines 271-278). The author leaves those two cases to the reader and this is reproduced as written. The organisation of the reduction, not its execution, is the content, so the claim is H2.
